name: Zimbabwe

claims.title: Great Zimbabwe is built
claims.summary: Ancestors of the Shona began raising the mortarless granite walls of Great Zimbabwe, which would become the largest stone city in sub-Saharan Africa and give the modern nation its name.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1000-great-zimbabwe-is-built, claim TL:ZWE:event:1000:great-zimbabwe-is-built, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Apex of the gold trade
claims.summary: At its height the city held perhaps 10,000–18,000 people and controlled a gold and ivory trade reaching the Swahili coast at Sofala and Kilwa; Chinese porcelain, Persian glass and a Kilwa coin have been excavated there.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1250-apex-of-the-gold-trade, claim TL:ZWE:event:1250:apex-of-the-gold-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline and abandonment
claims.summary: Great Zimbabwe was abandoned, probably owing to resource exhaustion and shifting trade routes, as the centre of power moved north toward the Zambezi and successor states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1450-decline-and-abandonment, claim TL:ZWE:event:1450:decline-and-abandonment, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Inscribed as a World Heritage Site
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribed Great Zimbabwe National Monument as a World Heritage Site, recognising it as a unique testimony to the Bantu civilisation of the Shona between the 11th and 15th centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1986-inscribed-as-a-world-heritage-site, claim TL:ZWE:event:1986:inscribed-as-a-world-heritage-site, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Mutapa empire
claims.summary: The Mutapa (Mwenemutapa) empire emerged toward the Zambezi, inheriting Great Zimbabwe's gold trade and ruling much of the northern plateau and parts of present-day Mozambique.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1450-rise-of-the-mutapa-empire, claim TL:ZWE:event:1450:rise-of-the-mutapa-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese intervention in the gold trade
claims.summary: Portuguese traders based at Sofala and on the Zambezi pressed into the interior, establishing fairs and interfering in Mutapa politics, steadily weakening the empire over the next century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1505-portuguese-intervention-in-the-gold-trade, claim TL:ZWE:event:1505:portuguese-intervention-in-the-gold-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Torwa state and Khami
claims.summary: In the south-west the Torwa state built its capital at Khami near present-day Bulawayo, continuing the stone-walling tradition in decorated terraces; Khami is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1450-the-torwa-state-and-khami, claim TL:ZWE:event:1450:the-torwa-state-and-khami, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Rozvi state under Changamire Dombo
claims.summary: Changamire Dombo founded the Rozvi state, absorbing the Torwa and expelling Portuguese fairs from the plateau around the 1690s; Rozvi power dominated the region until the Mfecane in the 1830s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1680-the-rozvi-state-under-changamire-dombo, claim TL:ZWE:event:1680:the-rozvi-state-under-changamire-dombo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ndebele settle the south-west
claims.summary: Mzilikazi led the Ndebele north during the Mfecane and established a centralised military kingdom around Bulawayo, dominating the south-western plateau and its Shona inhabitants.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1838-the-ndebele-settle-the-south-west, claim TL:ZWE:event:1838:the-ndebele-settle-the-south-west, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rudd Concession and the Pioneer Column
claims.summary: Lobengula signed the 1888 Rudd Concession granting mining rights to Rhodes's agents; Rhodes won a royal charter in 1889 and in 1890 the British South Africa Company's Pioneer Column occupied Mashonaland, raising the flag at Fort Salisbury on 13 September.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1888-rudd-concession-and-the-pioneer-column, claim TL:ZWE:event:1888:rudd-concession-and-the-pioneer-column, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Matabele War
claims.summary: Company forces invaded and destroyed the Ndebele kingdom; Lobengula fled and soon died, and the British South Africa Company annexed Matabeleland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1893-first-matabele-war, claim TL:ZWE:event:1893:first-matabele-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Chimurenga risings
claims.summary: The Ndebele and Shona rose against Company rule in revolts inspired in part by spirit mediums such as Nehanda and Kaguvi; the risings were crushed and their leaders executed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1896-first-chimurenga-risings, claim TL:ZWE:event:1896:first-chimurenga-risings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Southern Rhodesia becomes a self-governing colony
claims.summary: After a settler referendum, Company rule ended and Southern Rhodesia became a self-governing British colony, with land and political power reserved for the white minority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1923-southern-rhodesia-becomes-a-self-governing, claim TL:ZWE:event:1923:southern-rhodesia-becomes-a-self-governing, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Land Apportionment Act
claims.summary: Settler legislation formalised racial division of land, reserving the most productive areas for the white minority and restricting African landholding, a grievance that fuelled later nationalism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1930-land-apportionment-act, claim TL:ZWE:event:1930:land-apportionment-act, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of ZANU and ZAPU
claims.summary: African nationalism crystallised in two movements: ZAPU under Joshua Nkomo and the breakaway ZANU, soon led toward armed struggle by figures including Robert Mugabe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1963-founding-of-zanu-and-zapu, claim TL:ZWE:event:1963:founding-of-zanu-and-zapu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Unilateral Declaration of Independence
claims.summary: Ian Smith's Rhodesian Front declared independence from Britain to preserve white-minority rule; Britain and the UN refused recognition and imposed sanctions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1965-unilateral-declaration-of-independence, claim TL:ZWE:event:1965:unilateral-declaration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The liberation war (Second Chimurenga)
claims.summary: Guerrilla forces of ZANU (ZANLA) and ZAPU (ZIPRA), based in Mozambique and Zambia, waged an escalating war against the Rhodesian state through the 1970s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1972-the-liberation-war-second-chimurenga, claim TL:ZWE:event:1972:the-liberation-war-second-chimurenga, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lancaster House Agreement
claims.summary: Talks in London produced an agreement providing for a ceasefire, a new constitution and British-supervised elections, ending the war and opening the path to majority rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1979-lancaster-house-agreement, claim TL:ZWE:event:1979:lancaster-house-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence under Robert Mugabe
claims.summary: Zimbabwe became an internationally recognised independent state, with Mugabe's ZANU(PF) in power after winning the February 1980 election.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1980-independence-under-robert-mugabe, claim TL:ZWE:event:1980:independence-under-robert-mugabe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Gukurahundi massacres
claims.summary: The army's Fifth Brigade carried out massacres in Matabeleland and the Midlands targeting ZAPU supporters and Ndebele civilians; estimates of the dead range from several thousand to over twenty thousand. The campaign ended with the 1987 Unity Accord.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-1983-the-gukurahundi-massacres, claim TL:ZWE:event:1983:the-gukurahundi-massacres, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fast-track land reform
claims.summary: The government backed often-violent seizures of white-owned commercial farms; the disruption, with drought and sanctions, helped trigger a severe economic collapse.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-2000-fast-track-land-reform, claim TL:ZWE:event:2000:fast-track-land-reform, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hyperinflation and dollarisation
claims.summary: Inflation reached among the highest rates ever recorded, peaking in late 2008; in 2009 Zimbabwe abandoned its own currency for foreign ones such as the US dollar.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-2008-hyperinflation-and-dollarisation, claim TL:ZWE:event:2008:hyperinflation-and-dollarisation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mugabe forced from power
claims.summary: After a military intervention and the threat of impeachment, Robert Mugabe resigned after thirty-seven years in power, and Emmerson Mnangagwa became president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zimbabwe: From the great medieval stone city of the Shona, through the Mutapa and Rozvi states, the Ndebele kingdom, British colonisation as Southern Rhodesia, and a long liberation war to independence in 1980.", terralore.co/country/ZWE/chronicle#ev-2017-mugabe-forced-from-power, claim TL:ZWE:event:2017:mugabe-forced-from-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
